entries.title: the rules of reactions with several genes refer to the wrong genes
entries.why: Lines 61-63 renumber local indices with sequential strrep: for b2+b3 (local x(1)&x(2), geneInd [2 3]) step 1 gives 'x(2) & x(2)', step 2 gives 'x(3) & x(3)', while rxnGeneMat (line 60) is right; valid input, contradicts the rules/grRules intent.

entries.title: integerizeS is called with a matrix but needs a model structure
entries.why: Line 17 passes the matrix SeFull to integerizeS, whose signature (src/analysis/topology/integerizeS.m line 1) takes a model and reads model.S (line 38, not 39), so every documented call errors.

notes: integerizeS line is 38 not 39. Not recorded: the uni==0 branch closes fid at line 32 and again at line 45 (fclose of a closed id errors once line 17 is fixed), and uni is documented optional but has no default (line 21 errors when omitted).

entries.title: the outputFormat option always fails validation
entries.why: Line 84 validator calls strcmpi(acceptedTypes) with one argument, so any explicit 'outputFormat' value (including the documented 'mps') fails; the default is never validated.

entries.title: writeMatrix given as the first option is taken for a positional problem name
entries.why: 'writeMatrix' is missing from optionalArgumentList (line 57), so when it is the first optional argument lines 66-75 remap it positionally to problemName='writeMatrix', fileName=false, and the ischar validator (line 83) fails.

entries.title: vartype is dropped from the default output
entries.why: Real: line 206 (default writeMatrix=true, default solverParams) calls BuildMPS without the 'Integer'/'Binary' lists built at 186-187. But the writeMatrix help (lines 32-33) documents that the default writes 'only the Matrix, not the full problem', and writeMatrix=false (line 209) does pass vartype, so the caller gets what writeMatrix documents; only the .vartype text is imprecise.

entries.title: The zero vector is returned as the solution although it violates Aeq*x = beq
entries.why: Line 49 tests max(Aeq*0-beq)==0, true when beq>=0 has one zero entry (beq=[0;5]), so z=0 is returned at line 50 although Aeq*0 ~= beq; valid input, wrong solution.

entries.title: Empty inequality (or equality) block errors when the LP optimum is zero
entries.why: Line 49 evaluates polyhedron.Ain*zeros(n,1) without the isempty guard that LPSolve/L1Solve/ThetaL0 use (e.g. line 184); Ain=[] gives a dimension error, Ain=zeros(0,n) gives an empty operand to &&. findMinimalSetOfRxns passes Ain=[].

entries.title: Theta L0 iteration errors when the l1 solution has no positive entry
entries.why: With x=-1, line 142 min(sol(sol>0)) and line 149 theta_func(min(sol(sol>zero_precision)),...) are empty, so the && on line 149 errors; Aeq=1, beq=-1 is a valid LP whose l1 solution is negative.

entries.title: Output z is not assigned when every entry of the LP solution is below zeps
entries.why: When init_result=0 (all |x0|<=zeps) but optvalue~=0, the shortcut (49) is skipped and the while condition at line 71 (init_result>0) is false, so z is never assigned unless err_l1==1 (line 84); requesting z errors.

entries.title: Diagnostic output is printed unconditionally
entries.why: Lines 43 and 61 (err_init, err_l1) lack semicolons and line 87 is a bare toc; output only, no effect on results.

entries.title: text values of problemTypeParams.method have no effect for MIQP
entries.why: For MIQP, text .method values set lpmethod at lines 248-260, then the else branch of line 268 (line 302) unconditionally sets lpmethod=4 for any non-'LP' problemType, so the documented text values (lines 28-29) have no effect; numeric values set qpmethod and survive.

entries.title: An LPProblem without csense stops with an error
entries.why: Line 165 nMet=size(LPProblem.A) is a 1x2 vector and line 170 uses 1:nMet; on current MATLAB this errors (older releases used the first element). csense is documented optional (line 25) and the code intends to fill 'E'.

entries.title: The documented solution fields solver (every interface) and stat (ILOGsimple) are missing
entries.why: ILOGsimple (363-421) never sets .stat or .solver, tomlab_cplex (422-464) never sets .solver, and the status mapping (519) runs only for 'tomlab_cplex'; OUTPUT (lines 78-85) documents .stat and .solver.

notes: Entry 1 depends on MATLAB version: older releases took the first element of a vector colon operand.

entries.title: An LPProblem without csense stops with an error
entries.why: Same as the 2018 variant: line 155 nMet=size(A) (vector), line 160 LPProblem.csense(1:nMet,1)='E' errors on current MATLAB; csense documented optional and the code intends to default it.

entries.title: The IBM ILOG branch returns the objective of a maximisation with the wrong sign
entries.why: c=osense*LP.c (line 182); line 331 sets obj=-c=LP.c with sense 'maximize' (327) for osense=-1, objval=LP.c'x=10, then line 362 multiplies by osense giving -10. (Also for osense=1 the objective -LP.c is minimised, i.e. the wrong direction, not recorded.)

entries.title: theNorm 'zero' optimises the original objective in the wrong direction or reports it with the wrong sign
entries.why: Line 402 uses obj=c=osense*LP.c with sense 'maximize' (397) for osense=-1, so v3 is minimised (0); line 536 bounds v3 by 0*beta; line 587 reports -x'*c; for minimisation obj sign is flipped relative to LP.c'x.

entries.title: The cardinality solve prints the solution structure and a minimum-Euclidean-norm note
entries.why: Line 433 lacks a semicolon and lines 806-809 print the Euclidean-norm note for any nonzero minNorm regardless of theNorm/printLevel; console only.

notes: Additional, not recorded: in the non-card ILOG branch with osense=1 the objective -LP.c is minimised (line 331), i.e. the problem is optimised in the wrong direction.

entries.title: Data for a reaction not in the model, or duplicate data, stop with an error
entries.why: Lines 69 and 75 read the undefined variable printLevel (param.printLevel is set at 55), so any unmatched (locb==0) or duplicated exoMet.rxns errors, although lines 68-77 and 82 are written to tolerate them. (Not recorded: default relaxBounds=1 also reads undocumented model.lb_preconstrainRxns/ub_preconstrainRxns, lines 122-124.)

notes: Not recorded: default param.relaxBounds=1 reads model.lb_preconstrainRxns/ub_preconstrainRxns (lines 123-124), fields not documented as required.

entries.title: A problem type that GAMS does not list stops with an index error
entries.why: ismember('MINLP', problemTypes) returns position 0, never empty, so line 49 is always true and numTable(:,0) at line 50 errors; the else branch (52) shows the intended empty result.

entries.title: The existence of licememo.gms is never checked
entries.why: licememoFullPath (line 40) is a concatenated non-empty string, so isempty at 41 is never true and the error at 42 is unreachable; no file existence check. Message only, cosmetic.

entries.title: timelimit overrides TimeLimit although the help text says it is copied only when TimeLimit is absent
entries.why: Line 80 copies timelimit to TimeLimit unconditionally, contrary to the help text (lines 20-21: 'copied to .TimeLimit if .TimeLimit is absent').

entries.title: printLevel, feasTol and optTol are required although the fields are documented as optional
entries.why: Lines 182/194 read param.printLevel when OutputFlag/DisplayInterval are absent, 214 reads param.feasTol and 223 param.optTol without isfield checks; help says all fields optional, so setGurobiParam(struct()) errors.

entries.title: the warning for an unknown lpmethod names param.qpmethod
entries.why: Line 145 warning text says 'param.qpmethod' in the lpmethod branch; message only.

entries.title: The error for a parameter that is not allowed always names LP solvers
entries.why: Line 85 hard-codes 'for LP solvers' regardless of solverType; message only.

entries.title: solverType is documented as optional with default 'LP' but cannot be omitted
entries.why: INPUTS (line 9) say solverType is optional with default 'LP', but the signature is positional and line 80 always treats the first argument as solverType, so omitting it errors. Effectively a help-text error, but by the rule a documented-optional argument that cannot be omitted is unusable-option.

notes: Quarantine rests only on entry 2, a help-text error (USAGE and code agree that solverType is required). Correct by the rule, but the fix is likely a doc edit.

entries.title: The global solver parameters are ignored when no paramStructure is given
entries.why: Without paramStructure, line 66 sets overRideDefaults=0, so the global (CobraSolverState) values at lines 169-176 are never read, contradicting the documented priority (lines 2-7) that includes the global parameters.

entries.title: paramStructure 'default' returns the global values instead of the defaults
entries.why: Line 61 sets overRideDefaults=1 in the 'default' branch (a no-op since line 55 already set 1), so globals override the defaults; the help (24-25) and comment (56) say 'default' should return the script defaults.

entries.title: The structure output keeps the fields named in paramNames
entries.why: paramStructureOut starts as a copy of paramStructure (58) and lines 166/181 set the requested fields, so the output keeps them; OUTPUTS (31-32) document them removed. Behaviour contradicts the documented result on a valid call (doc likely the stale part).

entries.title: The invalid-parameters error message shows literal \n instead of line breaks
entries.why: error() is called with a single concatenated string (54-56), so '\n' is not interpreted; message only.

entries.title: param does not hold the additional (solver-specific) parameters
entries.why: param is rebuilt from defaultParams only (91-102) and non-COBRA fields stay only in solverOnlyParams; OUTPUTS (24) say param also holds 'any additional parameters'. Contradicts the documented output; all callers rely on the code, so the help is probably what is wrong, but by the rule this is wrong-result.

notes: Quarantine rests only on entry 2, which is probably a help-text error (all callers use solverOnlyParams). Correct by the rule.

entries.why: When no row has maxval>=BIG, lines 44-47 print 'Nothing to do' and return before any output is assigned, so callers requesting outputs (liftCouplingConstraints line 385-386, which does not guard this case) error; the message shows the intent to return C unchanged.

entries.title: The number of gradient evaluations is always reported as 1
entries.why: Ngmap is set to 1 at line 128 and never incremented although line 194 evaluates [hxk,ghxk]=mapp(xk) every iteration; out.Ngmap (237) is documented as total gradient evaluations and Stopping_Crit 5 (MaxNumGmapEval, StopCriterion case 5) can never trigger.

entries.title: A cell array with more than one column is compared element by element, so M is not m x m
entries.why: For a cell, line 50 calls unique(A,'stable') element-wise while N=size(A,1) (47); for a 1x3 cell IA/IC index elements, so M(1,bool)=1 at line 60 grows M to 1x2 and duplicateBool is 2x1, contradicting the documented m x m / m x 1 outputs for an m x n input.

entries.title: A char value with a quote gives a script that cannot run
entries.why: Line 33 writes the char value between quotes without doubling embedded quotes, so the generated file is invalid and does not recreate the value the help (lines 4-7) promises.

entries.title: A char matrix with more than one row is written column by column
entries.why: Line 33 fprintf('%s') on a multi-row char matrix writes its characters in column order as one row ('acbd'), so the value recreated differs.

entries.title: Numeric values lose their class and digits beyond the 15th
entries.why: Line 30 mat2str(val) uses 15-digit precision and no 'class' option, so pi loses digits and int8(5) is recreated as double 5; contradicts 'recreates those field values' (precision part is borderline, class loss is clear).

entries.title: A numeric array with more than two dimensions stops with an error and leaves the file open
entries.why: mat2str errors on N-D arrays (line 30), and the file opened at line 24 is not closed (no onCleanup; fclose only at 36); S documented as a struct of numeric/char fields.

entries.title: The confirmation is asked only on a jenkins home, the opposite of the documentation
entries.why: Line 20 condition is ~isempty(strfind(HOME,'jenkins')), i.e. it prompts only ON jenkins, the opposite of the comment at line 21 and the help ('blocks execution until confirmation').

entries.title: The optional input savepath cannot be used
entries.why: Line 64 saveas(ax, ...) uses ax, which exists only inside the local function plotHeatmapWithLabels (line 69), so providing savepath errors; line 63 cd(savepath) has already changed the session directory.

entries.title: The option saveFigures cannot be used
entries.why: Lines 421-422 build the file name from the undefined variable names (descriptions is computed at 411-415 instead), so saveFigures=1 errors after plotting.

entries.title: extraFluxes without otherFluxes stops with an error
entries.why: With extraFluxes given and otherFluxes empty, lines 241-244 use v2, which is defined only in the otherFluxes branch (186/193), so the call errors although both inputs are documented optional.

entries.title: predictedFluxes without lb and ub stops with an error
entries.why: lb/ub are documented variables of predictedFluxes (lines 13-14); without them, lines 170-173 use undefined measuredFluxes and x. Input outside the documentation, so limitation is right.

entries.title: param.metLookupTable without param.model stops with an undefined variable
entries.why: Lines 97 and 102 test membership in model.mets, but model is assigned only in the param.model branch (70); with only metLookupTable (documented 'either ... or/and', line 6) a matched compound errors.

entries.title: A compound whose name contains another compound's name receives that metabolite
entries.why: Line 73 uses contains(sumConc.metabolite_bmfl, mets{i}), so 'citrate' also selects 'isocitrate' and assigns cit[e]; the isocitrate pass (no [e] form, lines 76-77) does not overwrite it.

entries.title: The inactive proteins are those above the threshold
entries.why: Line 39 uses proteomicsEx>treshold, giving the proteins above the threshold as inactive, overlapping the active set (line 38 >=); evidently intended < treshold.

entries.title: The histogram marks the threshold at 2 whatever threshold is given
entries.why: Lines 29-30 draw the line and label at the constant x=2 instead of treshold; plot only.

entries.title: A system without java stops with an undefined variable options
entries.why: When java is missing, system('java') returns a non-1 code, so line 39 evaluates options.atomMapping, and options is not defined anywhere in the function (no inputs), so it errors instead of returning javaInstalled=false.

entries.title: An empty component of a multi-component charge layer stops with an error
entries.why: Lines 41-43 (and 52-53) strsplit the q/p layer on ';' and eval each part; standard InChI leaves uncharged components empty ('+1;'), and eval('') with an output inside the anonymous function errors.

entries.title: Element counts are assigned to the wrong elements on the combining path
entries.why: Line 50 appends setdiff(...) which returns the new elements sorted ({'C','Cl','H'}), but line 55 adds current_coefs in the formula-layer order using logical A, so coefficients land on the wrong elements (C2Cl3H2); the index output B is unused.

entries.title: A formula that loses all its hydrogen atoms keeps one H
entries.why: H coefficient 0 is printed as 'H0' (lines 58-64) and lines 71-79 replace 'H0' by 'H', so a fully deprotonated formula keeps one H (sulfate 'HO4S').

entries.title: replace = true stops with an error for every matched metabolite
entries.why: Line 88 assigns the char data2add to a cell field with () indexing (the non-replace branch at 102 uses {}), so replace=true errors on every match.

entries.title: A struct as inputData stops with an error
entries.why: Line 29 isfile(inputData) errors for a struct (text required) before the isstruct branch, and line 32 would pass the struct to readtable anyway; help (line 15) documents struct input.

entries.title: The labels inconsistentCharge and inconsistentFormula are swapped
entries.why: case 1 of line 121's switch means charge equal and formula different, but line 129 labels it 'inconsistentCharge' and case 3 (formula equal, charge different) 'inconsistentFormula'; labels swapped.

entries.title: A metabolite whose identifier contains mol after another character is reported missing
entries.why: Line 33 regexprep(names,'.mol','') treats '.' as any character, so 'amol.mol' becomes '' and the metabolite is reported missing although its file exists.

entries.title: A model without an HMDB field stops with an error
entries.why: hmdbIDs is assigned only if an hmdb field exists (133-136), unlike every other ID list which gets an empty default, and line 245 reads hmdbIDs{idx(1)} before checking sources, so any model without an HMDB field errors (borderline: the help lists metHMDBID among model fields, but the code's handling of all other ID fields shows they are meant to be optional).

entries.title: The documented source name lipidmass stops with an error
entries.why: The help (line 38) lists 'lipidmass' but the code only knows 'lipidmaps' (74, 78); line 382 removes all idMatrix columns while varNames (392) still includes 'lipidmass', so table() at 393 errors.

entries.title: The SMILES source is used only for metabolites that have an InChI
entries.why: Line 358 tests inchis{idx(1)} instead of smiles{idx(1)} before converting smiles (365), so a metabolite with SMILES but no InChI is skipped (and one with InChI but no SMILES is attempted).

notes: Entry 1 is borderline limitation vs error; entries 2 and 3 independently support quarantine.

entries.title: No selected MOL file stops with an undefined variable standardised
entries.why: standardised is assigned only inside the loop (207); when aMets is empty (no matching files) line 221 reads it undefined, while nonStandardised/InChIs are initialised at 108-109.

entries.title: The help text documents an optional input printWarning that the function does not have
entries.why: The help (line 16) documents an optional input printWarning, but the signature (line 1) has one input, so passing it errors with too many inputs. Essentially stale help text; by the rule a documented argument that fails when used is unusable-option.

notes: Quarantine rests only on stale help text for a nonexistent argument. Correct by the rule, but a doc fix would clear it.

entries.title: The input method is ignored, method 1 (cumomer) cannot be selected
entries.why: Line 50 tests nargin < 6 in a 5-input function, so method is always overwritten with 2; method=1 (documented line 24) is only used as the NaN fallback.

entries.title: A non-empty substrate label distribution glc stops with an error
entries.why: Line 34 calls convert_input, which does not exist in the repository, so every call with non-empty glc errors; with empty glc line 32 needs experiment.inputfrag, so the empty-experiment branches cannot run either.

entries.title: calcMDVfromSamp is called with four arguments, every non-empty sample set stops with an error
entries.why: Line 57 calls calcMDVfromSamp(model, xglc, samp, measuredMetabolites) with 4 arguments, but calcMDVfromSamp takes 3 (glc, points, experiment), so every non-empty samps errors.
